method: Developer and delegated read-only code audit, plus an executable preview diagnostic. Not the live discovery catalog; not written to runs/goals/backlog.json. Scores are reviewer estimates.

gaps.title: Make the preview tell the truth
gaps.label: Smallest repair
gaps.pitch: Scout is inside the car. Watch looks available. The click is refused. The action card should have said so first.
gaps.player: A reliable action preview lets the player plan without discovering restrictions through failed clicks.
gaps.exists: Issue already rejects in-car orders. LearnQuery already mirrors down, inside and busy gates, and its reads are pure.
gaps.gap: LearnQuery omits the in-car gate. A fresh-state diagnostic now reproduces preview accepted=true while Issue returns in-car.
gaps.next: Add and freeze a failing preview/Issue parity test, then repair the shared eligibility gate. No new game rule or asset is needed.
gaps.boundary: Fits the current engine-only writer boundary. The report reproduces the defect; it does not fix it.
checks: A boarded Scout gets in-car from both LearnQuery and Issue.
Watch and Listen retain their existing refusal precedence and supported targets.
Calling the preview changes no state hash, orders or logs.
On-foot orders still behave identically; regression tests remain green.

evidence.quote: rule: every order shows its full price before commit
public Answer LearnQuery(string agent, string verb, string target)

gaps.title: Make a turned café owner useful
gaps.label: Next substantive feature
gaps.pitch: A café owner knows their regulars. Turning them should reveal those people’s needs before Scout spends time listening.
gaps.player: One contact becomes an intelligence source, opening cheaper and better-informed approaches to other people.
gaps.exists: The people generator derives who each keeper knows. The rulebook already defines keeper.tips at mission start: reveal needs only.
gaps.gap: The simulation export omits that knowledge map; its loader does not accept it. Startup applies manual knowledge instead of evaluating keeper tips, and turned inputs address mission roles rather than arbitrary keeper IDs.
gaps.next: Carry the existing knowledge map into the simulation, accept turned keeper IDs, and apply the rulebook event once at mission start.
gaps.boundary: Requires people-export and input-schema integration outside the current sim/*.cs writer allowlist. Bound and review that adapter change before an autonomous write. No new balance numbers are needed.
checks: A turned keeper reveals exactly their workmates’ and regulars’ needs.
An unturned keeper reveals no needs.
Temperament, secrets and routine remain unknown; unrelated people stay unknown.
New inputs and learned knowledge participate in deterministic replay hashes.

evidence.quote: café owner tips needs before Scout listens

gaps.title: Give Continue a lasting consequence
gaps.label: Foundation for later work
gaps.pitch: The debrief can explain what happened. The next mission still needs a durable way to inherit it.
gaps.player: Contacts, needs, Trail and district Standing become the consequences the player lives with, not just the contents of a debrief.
gaps.exists: BetweenMissions already computes contact copies, replaced needs, Standing, cases and next security. Those calculations are not missing.
gaps.gap: The engine exposes those results as outputs, but a campaign layer does not consume and persist them into the next mission. Fresh starts rebuild state from site defaults and optional overrides.
gaps.next: Define a narrow, versioned campaign snapshot and a commit-once transition into mission 2. Start with contacts, needs, Trail and Standing; separate the wider calendar and world changes.
gaps.boundary: Needs an explicit transition contract and idempotency tests. Do not bundle every campaign mechanic or extra guard/camera placement into one agent task.
checks: Continue commits the mission result exactly once.
Mission 2 starts with projected contacts, needs, Trail and Standing.
Save/load reproduces the same next start and replay hashes.
Practice replay never commits rewards or consequences a second time.

evidence.quote: replay freely before Continue; after, the result stands.
No campaign layer runs yet: these are outputs.

gaps.title: Carry the wounds into tomorrow
gaps.label: Dependent follow-on
gaps.pitch: An operative who leaves injured should begin the next mission injured. Starting a new game currently restores the default health.
gaps.player: Surviving a fight has a lasting cost, and finding a doctor becomes a meaningful future choice.
gaps.exists: Combat already tracks damage, and the debrief exports the cell’s remaining health.
gaps.gap: The new-game constructor creates every operative at rulebook starting health. Start has no persisted per-operative health input.
gaps.next: Add validated health to the campaign snapshot and next-start state. Keep healing and calendar choices outside this first slice.
gaps.boundary: Depends on a campaign transition. Doctor healing rates, prices and scheduling need rulebook decisions; do not invent them in the carryover patch.
checks: An injured survivor keeps their exact remaining health next mission.
Healthy survivors stay healthy; invalid health is rejected.
Save/load and replay include per-operative health.
Downed and captured operatives have explicit transition handling.
